Following 18 months of research and development—50 per cent longer than the standard cycle—the creation of the RICH (RF Factory) Cartier Santeuil Skeleton watch was, in itself, the ultimate test of time and patience. In the replica watch industry, most products are typically brought to market within 12 months of project inception, in pursuit of a quicker return on investment. However, the RICH team chose a different path—they spent a full year and a half repeatedly dismantling the genuine timepiece, meticulously tackling the layout of the skeletonised movement’s bridges, the logic of gear meshing, and the curvature data for every curved surface of the case. This almost obsessive dedication stems from a profound understanding of Cartier’s language of skeletonisation: the Santos’s skeletonised aesthetic is not merely about removing metal to reveal the movement, but about visually constructing an architectural sense of geometric order. The transparency, sense of layering and the play of light and shadow created as light passes through the bridges of the original timepiece all required countless prototypes and refinements to approximate. The extra six months have resulted in a piece that dares to withstand the harshest scrutiny in every detail—for only a creation that withstands close examination under intense light can truly be called ‘hardcore’. Through this extraordinary development cycle, RICH has demonstrated to the industry what true craftsmanship entails.

The interchangeability of the steel bracelet is one of the most significant technical breakthroughs in this RICH creation. The structure of the Cartier Santos steel bracelet is renowned for its precision and complexity; each link is connected to the next via tiny pins and clasps, with extremely stringent tolerance controls. The RICH team has achieved full interchangeability with the original links whilst maintaining the same level of precision in the openwork craftsmanship—this is not merely a matter of approximate dimensions, but rather ensures that the length, width, thickness and pin hole positions of every link match the genuine article to the micrometre. Once assembled, the overall lines are smooth and seamless, with the difference virtually indistinguishable to the naked eye. Even more astonishing is that the three core components of the quick-release system—the push-buttons, locking pins and sliders—are also perfectly interchangeable with the original parts. The quick-release mechanism is key to the Santos’s wearing experience, determining both the smoothness of strap changes and the security of the lock. RICH has not only replicated the curvature and press travel of the push-buttons in appearance, but has also matched the genuine article in terms of the tension coefficient of the internal springs and the wear resistance of the locking pins. This means that even when comparing the feel on the wrist, the average watch enthusiast would find it extremely difficult to detect any difference. This replacement-grade steel bracelet embodies the RICH team’s in-depth research into structural engineering and their confidence in the industry.

The precision of the moulding for the openworked bridge plates is an achievement of which the RICH team is justifiably proud; however, it must be objectively acknowledged that, when it comes to the extremely fine brushed finish on the back of the movement, the original manufacturer still has a slight edge. This discrepancy is primarily evident at a microscopic level, barely perceptible to the naked eye—the genuine watch maintains a consistent and delicate brushed finish even in the most concealed corners of the bridge’s reverse side, whereas RICH has not yet fully matched the original manufacturer’s exacting standards in the finishing of these non-visible surfaces. The RICH team never shies away from these objective shortcomings; on the contrary, they choose to address them candidly at the time of launch, as only by acknowledging their limitations can they continue to improve. It is precisely this spirit of self-reflection that drives the brand to continually elevate its craftsmanship. However, in the two core areas of steel bracelets and structural design, RICH possesses absolute confidence within the industry—substitute-grade precision, a parts system fully compatible with the original, and perfect adaptation to quick-release mechanisms. These tangible strengths are more than sufficient to make the RICH Skeleton Santos stand out amongst its peers. Acknowledging gaps without feeling inferior, and possessing strengths without becoming arrogant—this is RICH’s approach to its creations, and it is also a mark of respect for its customers.

The distinctive star-shaped screw at the 5 o’clock position on the case back is the core anti-counterfeiting feature that sets RICH apart from other standard versions on the market; it is also a subtle detail through which the brand pays homage to the genuine article. This special screw is not positioned at random; in the genuine watch, it serves the dual functions of securing the case back and preventing accidental disassembly. The depth and angle of its star-shaped slots, as well as the curvature of the chamfer on the screw head, are all subject to strict manufacturing standards. To perfectly replicate this feature, the RICH team specially commissioned high-precision machining tools and conducted repeated tests on the feel of the slot engagement to ensure that the tool fits naturally during disassembly, without slipping or jamming. It is worth noting that the full set of eight case back and bezel screws are fully interchangeable with the original manufacturer’s parts, meaning that RICH has achieved a level of precision—in both external dimensions and thread accuracy—that allows for direct replacement of the original components. Although small, screws serve as a crucial indicator of a watch’s craftsmanship—standard versions often use generic screws that are similar in shape but lack precision in the finer details; RICH’s star-shaped screws, however, are identical to the genuine article in every respect, from the sharpness of their edges to the finish of their surfaces. This exclusive feature gives the RICH Skeletonised Santos a unique identity amongst its many competitors.

Building on Cartier’s tradition of skeletonisation, RICH has achieved a seamless continuity in its aesthetic approach, from geometric composition to functional layout. The reason the skeletonised design of the Cartier Santos is considered a classic lies in its transformation of the movement’s bridge structure into a form of visual architectural beauty—the orientation of the bridges, the arrangement of the gears and the positioning of the ruby bearings all combine to form a precise mechanical masterpiece. During the development process, the RICH team carried out 3D scans and data comparisons of every curve in the bridges and every position of the gear train on the genuine model, ensuring that the transparency ratios of the openworked areas are identical to those of the original. Furthermore, the sapphire used for the crown is of Swiss original-factory grade; its depth of colour, the cutting angles of its curved surface, and the refractive effects when light passes through all meet the same standards as the genuine article. The curvature of the case and the direction of the brushed finish have been reproduced on a 1:1 scale – from the lugs to the bezel, the direction and thickness of every brushed line strictly adhere to the original manufacturer’s craftsmanship, ensuring the same interplay of light and shadow is presented under different lighting angles. This ultimate pursuit of aesthetic detail makes the RICH Skeleton Santos visually almost indistinguishable from the genuine article, truly achieving a perfect balance of form and spirit.

The rounded chamfering of the strap edges reflects RICH’s profound commitment to wearing comfort. The steel straps of the Cartier Santos are renowned for their bold style, but if the edges are not properly finished, prolonged wear can easily cause discomfort to the skin. In the final stage of steel bracelet production, the RICH team has introduced an additional chamfering process—using a micro-curved polishing technique to remove sharp edges, ensuring that the sides of each link have a soft and smooth texture. This results in a comfortable, friction-free fit that does not dig into the skin, offering thoughtful comfort even to wearers with slender wrists. At the same time, the clasp’s fastening precision and tension control are fully aligned with the craftsmanship standards of the genuine article. As one of the most frequently used components, the clasp’s resistance when opening, the crisp sound upon closing, and its stability once locked all directly influence the overall wearing experience. RICH has meticulously fine-tuned the thickness and bend angle of the spring plates within the clasp’s internal structure to ensure that every opening is smooth and firm, with no looseness whatsoever once closed. These seemingly inconspicuous refinements are precisely what distinguish a ‘crude replica’ from a ‘masterpiece’—it is in the details that true quality is revealed.

We use copper-free tungsten steel alloy to make the case. There is no steel coating on the surface, so it will never peel or fade. Those who are familiar with the weighing tungsten-copper watches know that products from other factories will have a steel coating on the surface. After wearing them for just one month, the coating will flake off. Why do they use the steel coating process? Because the gold plating solution currently available on the market is developed for stainless steel. They cannot directly electroplate gold on tungsten-copper alloy, so they use the steel coating to solve the problem of electroplating gold. After all, electroplating gold is the cheapest process. But they never expected that the steel layer and tungsten-copper alloy are not compatible: thermal expansion and contraction will cause the outer layer of stainless steel to deform and flake off. In addition, tungsten-copper alloy contains a large amount of copper elements, which is prone to rust and oxidation, and the material is extremely unstable!!!

Let's take another example: Some factories did not adopt the surface steel coating process but instead used a more expensive gold coating technique. However, their products still faded and peeled off after being worn for two months. This is because their tungsten-copper alloy still contains a large amount of copper (adding copper is to reduce the hardness of tungsten so that it can be processed into precision parts). But when watch owners wear them, they are bound to sweat. When sweat reacts with the copper, bubbles will form under the gold layer, eventually causing fading and peeling. Are all watches with tungsten weights doomed to peel off and fade, and have a short lifespan?

The problem of fading and peeling has long plagued the entire industry. Now, it has finally been completely overcome by the research of UMI Studio!! We were the first in the industry to develop an alloy of tungsten steel without copper. However, tungsten steel has extremely high hardness, and traditional techniques are difficult to process it into precision watch parts. Therefore, we spared no expense and introduced a five-axis CNC machine tool to process all the parts. Due to the hardness of the material and the difficulty in controlling tolerances, each processed part (especially each section of the watch strap) needs to be manually polished by experienced masters to eliminate the tolerances. Although the output is low, we firmly refuse to accept compromise products!!

At the same time, we adopt the electroplating nickel process to add an anti-oxidation base layer on the surface of tungsten steel alloy parts, preventing the tungsten steel case from coming into contact with the air. The Swiss original movement can maintain a bright color for decades, which is precisely due to the nickel plating process. After electroplating nickel, our tungsten steel case is also treated with the most expensive gold plating process for watches currently available, making the wristwatch present a true gold luster. The entire watch is made using the true gold plating process, wrapping all the joint gaps of the parts in a 360-degree manner, and there is no exposed white color at the gaps between the case and the strap. The special gold plating liquid is specially formulated to make the final rose gold color exactly the same as the original, without any color difference, achieving a perfect level of replacement!!!

This is not all! After completing the gold plating process for the watch, we also applied the latest cutting-edge technology, the Swiss PVD coating technology (the same process as the gold-plated watches from Longines in Switzerland), to cover the surface of the watch with a hard and transparent protective film, which delays the wear of the gold plating layer. Therefore, we can solemnly promise to our friends who own the watches: If the gold color fades within three years, we will replace it free of charge. All the 5712 models produced by the UMI studio come with a certificate of gold content detection for the watch, and the materials are genuine and reliable, so there is no need to worry about verification!!!

The 5712 series is equipped with a truly groundbreaking super integrated Cal.240 PS IRM C LU movement. The movement contains as many as 265 components and features an ultra-thin planar hairspring, with an oscillation frequency of 21,600 times per hour. All parameters are benchmarked against the original 240 movement. (Unlike the common fake movement covers and fake pearl arbor techniques seen in the market) All functions of our 5712 can be perfectly realized: the same power reserve duration, genuine lunar phase function, calendar function, small seconds function, power display function, and dual quick adjustment buttons, etc.!!!

We have made a complete upgrade to the strap and clasp: the logo is deeply engraved, and a new expandable and adjustable clasp is included. The hinge structure is developed by replicating the original Patek Philippe Nautilus strap. It achieves a soft and comfortable fit similar to the genuine product. Unlike other replica strap products on the market, ours feels as soft as a bracelet when worn. Our product outshines all other replica versions currently available on the market. The angle of the rotating head pin is exactly the same as the original, and the sound when the clasp opens and closes is exactly the same as the original!

To achieve the highest level of detail restoration, we have also modified the iconic beak-shaped case and the real center axis of the hands that all watch enthusiasts have been eagerly awaiting. We have paired it with a custom gradient brown dial: at different light conditions and angles, the edge of the dial will naturally transition from black to brown. On the lug lines — matched lug position with even, flowing polished bevels. The smoothness of the lug lines directly affects the watch's overall look. DDF focused here on the polished edge, using CNC engraving combined with hand finishing to create even, arc-shaped polished chamfers along the four lug edges. Through the sapphire back, this hefty rotor turns smoothly, its edges finely chamfered and polished.

On this base, fine engraving renders a leaf-shaped motif whose proportions match the original, with clear edges and flowing lines. The rotor edge also has an angled polished bevel; this beveled edge reflects a bright halo as the rotor turns, further enhancing the view of the movement's reverse and ensuring every detail withstands scrutiny.
